appraisal_events.evidence: j'ai comme nom de guerre la princesse de Luxembourg ! ... C'est agréable d'avoir ici une promiscuité avec cette espèce de Baronne d'Ange ... Mme de Luxembourg, nièce du roi d'Angleterre et de l'empereur d'Autriche, et Mme de Villeparisis parurent toujours ... deux drôlesses de l'espèce de celles dont on se gare difficilement dans les villes d'eaux.
appraisal_events.explanation: The bâtonnier's mocking anecdote, generalized by the narrator into a durable pattern, treats the princesse de Luxembourg and Mme de Villeparisis as if they were disreputable, courtesan-like women, despite their high birth; the narrator frames this as the outsiders' chimeric "malentendu" rather than a truth he endorses.

status_effects.explanation: She is locally likened to a disreputable, courtesan-like figure by the bâtonnier's joke and the narrator's generalizing comment, even though the framing marks this as a misperception rather than fact.
The narrator explicitly extends the same "drôlesse" comparison to Mme de Villeparisis, so she shares in the same local diminishment through association with the princesse de Luxembourg.

ambiguities: The mockery of the princesse de Luxembourg and Mme de Villeparisis as "drôlesses" is explicitly framed by the narrator as a persistent misunderstanding ("malentendu") stemming from the bourgeois/legal milieu's chimeric view of the aristocracy, not as the narrator's own endorsed judgment; the diminishment is real within the passage but its truth-status is deliberately undercut.
